developments: Bitcoin rebounded from its overnight low of $55,100 to a high of about $60,880 on Kraken in the 13:00 UK hour and traded near $59,950 at 16:30 UK, up about 7% since the morning edition.
ZEC recovered more strongly, from about $685 at 06:00 UK to a high near $806, and traded near $785, up about 12% since the morning edition.
Total 24-hour liquidations reached about $2.67 billion, Bitcoin.com News reported, citing CoinGlass, and US spot bitcoin ETFs lost more than $1.25 billion from Tuesday to Friday.
briefing.changed: This morning Bitcoin had just broken its summer low and the question was whether forced selling had run out. Since then it has climbed back above the old $57,700 low and briefly above $60,000, so the break now looks like a weekend overshoot, though US markets have not yet traded on it.
briefing.question: Does the rebound above the old summer low hold when US stocks and ETFs reopen on Monday, after the Nasdaq's 5.3% fall on Friday?
briefing.watch: Sunday evening's US stock futures open (about 23:00 UK) and Monday's US open at 14:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin claws back to $60,000 after weekend flush
lead.standfirst: Bitcoin recovered nearly 10% from its overnight low on Saturday, briefly topping $60,000 again, after a wave of forced selling took it to its lowest level since September 2024.
body: Bitcoin rose to about $60,880 on Kraken in the 13:00 UK hour on Saturday, Kraken data showed, from a low of $55,100 in the early morning. It traded near $59,950 at 16:30 UK time, about 7% above the level at the morning edition.

Reuters reported Bitcoin up about 2.1% at $60,192 at 15:16 UK time. Bitcoin.com News said the overnight fall had come with about $2.67 billion of leveraged positions liquidated in 24 hours, about $1.3 billion of it in Bitcoin, according to CoinGlass.
The rebound left Bitcoin back above the June-July low near $57,700, which it broke overnight. Zcash rose further, from about $685 to a high near $806 on Kraken, before easing to about $785.

The bounce followed a heavy week on Wall Street. Decrypt reported that the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% on Friday and about 10% over the week, while Nvidia dropped 14% on the day and closed 47.5% below its October record. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost more than $1.25 billion from Tuesday to Friday, Bitcoin.com News reported.
US markets reopen on Monday, the first chance for stock and ETF investors to react to the weekend's moves.

headline: Bitcoin rebounded from its $55,100 overnight low to briefly top $60,000 and traded near $59,950, back above the broken summer low. ZEC rose about 12% to near $785, but US markets have yet to react.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition, Saturday the twenty first of November. Bitcoin has bounced hard. After falling to about fifty five thousand one hundred dollars overnight, it climbed back above sixty thousand around two in the afternoon UK time and is now near fifty nine thousand nine hundred and fifty, about seven percent up since this morning. Zcash rose about twelve percent to near seven hundred and eighty five dollars. The test comes on Monday, when US markets reopen after Friday's five percent fall in the Nasdaq. The next big event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin rebounds to $60,880 high, back above the broken summer low
stories.why: Kraken showed Bitcoin climbing from $55,100 to about $60,880 in the 13:00 UK hour, and near $59,950 at 16:30 UK. Reuters had it up about 2.1% at $60,192 at 15:16 UK. The new evidence changes this morning's picture: the June-July low near $57,700 has been reclaimed within hours of breaking.

note.read: A fast recovery after a liquidation flush in thin weekend trading fits the pattern of a forced-selling overshoot rather than fresh spot selling.
note.alt: Weekend rebounds on thin volume can also fade once US stock and ETF investors return; the Nasdaq's fall and ETF outflows have not reversed.
note.change: Holding above about $57,700 through Monday's US session would support the overshoot reading; a return below it would point to the selling resuming.

stories.title: ZEC jumps about 12% to near $785
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC rising from about $685 in the 06:00 UK hour to a high near $806 in the 13:00 UK hour, then near $785 at 16:30 UK. That is about 12% since the morning edition, against about 7% for Bitcoin, and back above Friday night's level of about $758.

note.read: ZEC is still moving at well over Bitcoin's pace in both directions, so its rebound reflects the same weekend swing amplified.
note.alt: ZEC holding above $678 while Bitcoin fell further this morning hinted its own selling was slowing before the wider bounce.
note.change: ZEC falling back faster than Bitcoin on Monday would show its high-beta pattern is still in charge.

stories.title: Liquidations reach about $2.67 billion; Nvidia closed 47.5% below its record
stories.why: Bitcoin.com News, citing CoinGlass, put 24-hour liquidations at about $2.67 billion, about $1.3 billion in Bitcoin, up from about $2.4 billion this morning. Decrypt reported the Nasdaq fell 5.3% on Friday and about 10% on the week, with Nvidia down 14% on Friday to $125.53. The new evidence is the scale of the AI-stock repricing behind Friday's sell-off.
stories.caveat: This morning's edition, citing Bitcoin Magazine, gave Nvidia's Friday fall as about 12.5% and the Nasdaq's as about 5%; Decrypt's later figures are 14% and 5.3%.

note.read: Crypto has bounced on its own over the weekend while the equity sell-off that started it has not been tested again.
note.alt: Liquidation totals rise as the 24-hour window rolls; the latest count may include the rebound's short squeeze as well as the earlier flush.
note.change: Calm US stock futures on Sunday evening would reduce the risk of a second wave.

stories.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost more than $1.25 billion from Tuesday to Friday
stories.why: Bitcoin.com News reported more than $1.25 billion of net outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs over Tuesday to Friday, including $582 million on Thursday, $541 million of it from BlackRock's IBIT. Friday's single-day figure was still not confirmed by a source we could read.

stories.title: Bitcoin Core patches node-stalling bug found by an AI scanner
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that repeating one transaction ID 50,000 times could stall a node for over a dozen seconds per message. Bitcoin Core rated it medium severity and shipped fixes on Friday in versions 30.5 and 31.3; the affected code dates from version 29.0. It was found by Loupe, an AI-agent scanner from Block's Spiral team. Relevant to anyone running a node, such as on the Pi.

stories.title: Chainflip vault drained of $4.86 million; FLIP down 34%
stories.why: The Block reported an attacker drained about $4.86 million in ETH, USDC and USDT from Chainflip's Ethereum vault at about 07:10 UK, apparently using a valid signature from its signing key rather than a code bug. Chainflip paused the protocol and FLIP fell about 34%. Chainflip is a cross-chain swap venue, a reminder of the risk in bridges.

stories.title: Ether treasury firm BTCS flags $54 million Aave loan risk
stories.why: CoinDesk reported that Nasdaq-listed BTCS told the SEC its Aave debt was about $54 million on 19 November. CoinDesk's own estimate puts liquidation near $1,450 per ether against about $1,730 on Saturday. It shows how the sell-off is pressing on leveraged crypto treasury companies.
stories.caveat: The liquidation price is CoinDesk's estimate, not a company disclosure.

explained.title: Why a market can snap back after a liquidation flush
body: When prices fall fast, leveraged long bets are closed automatically, and each forced sale pushes the price lower and triggers the next. Once most of that leverage is gone, there are few forced sellers left, so even modest buying can lift the price quickly.

Traders who bet on further falls can then be squeezed in turn, adding to the rebound. That is why a sharp drop and a sharp bounce often come together, and why the real test is whether ordinary buyers stay once the forced trades are done.

investigating: How large were Friday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflows on their own? Evidence: SoSoValue or Farside daily totals; the pages we tried today could not be read.
Is today's rebound built on fresh buying or short covering? Evidence: Bitcoin futures open interest and funding rates on Sunday compared with Saturday morning.
Will Monday's US session confirm the bounce? Evidence: Nasdaq and Nvidia moves and Monday's ETF flow figures.
